title: Lead pocket brief — PM/Eng 1:1 (API, Console, Dedicated, Private)
content:
Context:
Quick sync with Rohan (eng lead) before roadmap commit. Focus: small set of operational changes we want to land next 6 weeks that affect API latency, Console rollout UX, and Dedicated/Private routing policies. Need alignment on tradeoffs: developer ergonomics vs. latency SLOs vs. cost.

Agenda (30 min):
1) Quick wins (5m) — list + owners
2) Routing & fallback policy update (10m) — behavior for Dedicated burst -> hosted fallback, KV cache re-use, metrics to validate
3) Console rollout checklist (7m) — canary gating, telemetry flags, UX copy follow-up
4) Decisions & blockers (5m) — resource commits, infra work, any support needed from product/legal

Metrics snapshot to call out (bring these figures):
- Hosted API p50/p95 token latency for gen endpoints: 45ms / 210ms (last 7d) — note spikes during 18:00–20:00 PT
- Dedicated pools: 99% of requests under SLA for committed customers except pool-12 at 99.2% — likely preempt/queue contention
- Console feature flag adoption: 2% of accounts on new rollout; conversion from canary ~0.6
- Cost per 1k tokens for q4 baseline: $0.95 hosted; optimized quantized model target reduces to ~$0.65

Prep questions for Rohan (engineer):
- Routing: how feasible is a soft-fallback that preserves KV cache semantics? (risk: cache miss/unwarm)
- Autoscale knobs: can we expose a predictive scale factor based on request rate window (5m) without adding oscillation? Who owns the backfill logic?
- Dedicated burst capacity: what's estimate to add an extra 10% headroom for reserved pools (effort & infra cost)?
- Console telemetry: what minimal metrics do you need from frontend to assert rollout health? (token-level latency, follow ups, user-visible errors)

Decisions I want to push for in this meeting:
- Approve a 3-week dedicated spike to prototype soft-fallback with KV cache preservation; budget: 0.25 FTE infra + 0.5 FTE runtime
- Ship Console canary gating with simplified telemetry (no full tracing) if we get p95 under threshold for 48h in canary accounts
- Prioritize pool-12 investigation (SRE + runtime) in next sprint if we can get it to 99.8% with configuration tweak vs. code change

Current blockers / signals:
- SRE flagged pool-12 preemption events tied to kernel-level driver on GPU hosts (ticket INF-3499) — needs eng time or temporary routing exclusion
- UX copy for fallback UI is delayed (Maya on it) — don't want to ship UX that promises incorrect guarantees
- Data retention policy question from Legal about Private rollout logs (loop in security/compliance)

Action item template (to capture in meeting):
- Action: prototype plan for soft-fallback w/ KV preservation — Owner: Rohan — Due: 2024-11-25
- Action: shallow observability spec for Console canary — Owner: Maya — Due: 2024-11-20
- Action: triage INF-3499, propose mitigation (routing exclude / kernel patch) — Owner: SRE (Leah) + Rohan — Due: 2024-11-19
- Action: update pricing impact note for quantized vs baseline — Owner: me (Aisha) — Due: 2024-11-22

Talking points / persuasion hooks (notes to self):
- Emphasize customer SLA commitments for Dedicated customers — losing predictability is higher cost than small infra spend now.
- Position soft-fallback as reversible feature behind a flag; risk-limited and measurable.
- For Console canary, call out developer feedback loop: faster rollout = faster bug detection and metric-driven rollback.

Parking lot (if we have time):
- Longer-term: model-variant routing by cost-band (warm/cheap/expensive) — sketch in backlog
- Explore fine-grained token billing telemetry for top 20 customers

Meeting note placeholders (capture during 1:1):
- Notes: 
- Decisions made:
- Follow-ups assigned:

Personal reminders (scratch):
- Bring cost delta table (quantized vs float) — small table by bucket sizes
- Print excerpt of INF-3499 log sample to show to Rohan
- Flag legal question to security slack thread after meeting (cc: Priya)
